messages:
sanjay: Auditor asked for sample evidence with pseudonymized user IDs + KMS access logs for Jan 1–Jan 14. Want guidance on what to include and redaction approach. @elaine can you advise?
elaine: We can provide role-binding snapshots, Kubernetes audit logs (filtered), and S3 access events. For pseudonymization we usually HMAC user IDs with a per-audit salt stored offline. That way we can show consistent pseudonyms across artefacts without revealing PII.
matt: For KMS evidence, auditor typically wants crypto operation records (Encrypt/Decrypt/Generate/AsymmetricSign) and key metadata (key version, creation time). Cloud KMS admin activity entries + CloudTrail/CloudAudit logs are fine.
auditor_jan: Correct — we need proof of key usage and who requested it. Pseudonymization is acceptable if you can demonstrate chain-of-custody: mapping sealed and only released under defined process. Also need retention/backup policy for the salt.
sanjay: Can we include region and project but redact IP addresses? Auditor: region is important for jurisdiction.
elaine: Yes, keep region and project id. Remove full IPs and replace with CIDR /24 or just "REDACTED_NETWORK". Provide a note describing redaction rules.
auditor_jan: That's ok. Also please include a sample of the mapping process (sealed envelope) — e.g., signed and hashed manifest proving the pseudonym mapping existed at time X.
matt: We can create a manifest file with HMAC of the mapping and sign it with an ops key. Something like:
```
manifest.json: { "generated_at": "2025-01-15T18:00:00Z", "mapping_hmac": "sha256:HMACVALUE", "salt_hash": "sha256:..." }
```
We store the mapping in an encrypted bucket and provide a signature for the manifest.
sanjay: What about vulnerability triage items that intersect with this period? Auditor wants links to incident tickets that affected key material or RBAC changes.
elaine: Include a filtered list of incidents (ids, summary, status) and a short note if any playbook steps touched KMS or role bindings. No need to include full incident chat logs — just a reference pointer and exported timeline.
auditor_jan: We need evidence that RBAC changes were approved and documented. Screenshots or exported audit trail of the IAM console / git commits for infra-as-code changes are good.
matt: For infra-as-code, we can provide the git commit hash, PR approval history, and the deployment job logs that applied the change. Redact any reviewer emails.
ops-bot: evidence-packager: bundle ready at s3://redwood-audit/evidence/1769998888-pseudonym-sample.zip (size: 42 MB). MD5: 3b2d9f4a8c6f1e7d9e4a2b1c0f123456
sanjay: Great — can someone draft a one-pager describing redaction and mapping custody we can send the auditor? @elaine
elaine: I'll draft and attach the manifest/signature steps + a short checklist for reviewers. Expect a PR by EOD. :+1:
auditor_jan: Thanks — once we get the bundle and the one-pager we'll validate sampling. If you can include a tiny CSV (10 rows) showing pseudonym -> pseudonym-hash and the HMAC manifest, that helps the review without exposing PII.
sanjay: Sounds good. I'll coordinate packaging and the sealed mapping handoff process.
elaine: tagging: #evidence-runbook updated with these redaction rules and the HMAC workflow.
matt: FYI — I'll also add a QA step to the packager to ensure no IPs or full emails slip through.
ops-bot: deploy-bot: evidence-packager job 4521 completed by matt at 2025-01-16T09:12:00Z.
auditor_jan: Quick follow-up — retention policy for the salt that creates pseudonyms? How long is it kept and who has access?
elaine: Salt is kept in a sealed KMS-encrypted bucket with access limited to the compliance vault team; retention is 7 years as per the evidence retention policy. We will include ACL and KMS key policy snapshot in the bundle.
sanjay: Perfect. I'll mark this thread as actioned once PR and bundle are uploaded. Thanks everyone.
